issues.issue: Did the RAD err in applying the internal flight alternative (IFA) test?
issues.applicant_position: IFA concept subverts the Convention's spirit; RAD misapplied the 'serious possibility' test by requiring proof persecution was impossible.
issues.respondent_position: IFA is inherent in the refugee definition; RAD applied the test correctly and did not require proof of impossibility.
issues.result_quote: The RAD did not err in its identification and application of the IFA test.

issues.issue: Did the RAD make unreasonable findings of fact on Multan as an IFA?
issues.applicant_position: Multan was not viable; he was a prominent community member at risk, and Sunni Tehreek could locate him there.
issues.respondent_position: Mixed evidence showed only a mere possibility of harm; applicant was not a prominent leader; no evidence of tracking.
issues.result_quote: the RAD acted reasonably within its fact-finding role in resolving ambiguities in the evidence

issues.issue: Were the RPD and RAD processes procedurally fair in raising Multan as an IFA during the hearing?
issues.applicant_position: Notice of an IFA must come before the hearing and name the specific IFA; evidence on it was unobtainable.
issues.respondent_position: Clear notice during the hearing, with a chance to respond, is sufficient, and was given here.
issues.result_quote: In any event, in this case the RPD clearly raised Multan as a potential IFA during the hearing.
